findings.description: CONFIRMED shape bug. Every document in collection `state` is stored as {v:...} except stravaSnapshot, whose top-level keys are activities/syncedAt/via. applyRemoteSnapshot() at the sync layer returns early on `if (!data || typeof data !== "object" || !("v" in data)) return;`, so the Strava document is dropped before it ever reaches localStorage. It is the ONLY ingest path (initSync -> onSnapshot -> applyRemoteSnapshot), so a fresh Strava sync could never reach this card and it silently fell back to a Sep 7 seed. Fixed at the READER, not the sync engine: new stravaDoc() accepts both {v:{activities,...}} and {activities,...}; used by renderStravaActivity, the LIVE_FEED_ISO 'Strava activity' stamp and Kevin's live-dashboard context line. Smoke-tested under a DOM shim against: no document, unwrapped, wrapped, null, [], {}, "string", activities:"nope", and rows containing null/number — no throw in any case.

findings.description: A SYNCHRONOUS throw from window.claude.use kills the entire dashboard. `(function initSync(){ ... window.claude.use("db").then(...).catch(...) })()` guards only the PROMISE; the call itself is unguarded, so a throw propagates out of the top-level IIFE and every statement below it — every render, every safeRun — never executes. Measured under the harness: 0 of 318 container ids received innerHTML, i.e. a completely blank deck. This is the same failure class as the 2026-09-03 CI-log regression (a ReferenceError on the 1 s tick blanking Market Snapshot and everything below it). findings.description: take() returns early on `!m.id`, so any relayed message without an id is discarded with no record anywhere — not a console warning, not SHAPE_MISMATCH, not the Ops Radar. findings.system: lsSetLocal(key, value) — command-deck.html:6647 — and LS_UNAVAILABLE in lsGetSeeded — command-deck.html:6725
findings.description: A failing localStorage WRITE is completely invisible. lsSetLocal's catch is empty and LS_UNAVAILABLE is only ever set from a failing READ inside lsGetSeeded, so with setItem throwing the page still rendered all 318 containers, raised 0 console warnings and set LS_UNAVAILABLE=false. The read path is handled correctly (getItem throwing sets LS_UNAVAILABLE=true and raises the 'Local storage is unavailable in this view' alert), which is exactly why the write path reads as a healthy day. Anything Steven types into a panel is lost on reload with no warning.

While dbReady is false, any key that already has a queued local write is skipped entirely ("local is newer; it flushes next"). The isaLine branch itself calls syncKeyToDb, so in local-only mode the FIRST isaLine change queues a pending write and every later isaLine change in the same session is discarded. Measured with a 200-change burst carrying two conflicting isaLine arrays: db-connected stored 88 of 90 messages; local-only stored 48 of 90. The merge is otherwise well behaved: replaying the identical burst rewrote 0 keys (changed=false), so it is idempotent and cannot loop the 30 s location.reload() throttle.

findings.system: renderPanelStamps() — command-deck.html:20372 — the debounced re-render behind every lsSet
findings.description: renderPanelStamps is the single slowest render on a clean baseline (44 ms of a 1070 ms page) and it is re-run on a 400 ms debounce after EVERY recordSectionEdit, i.e. after every keystroke-driven save. Under the routineHealth volume payload it rose to 82 ms. It re-runs document.querySelectorAll('.panel[data-page]') and walks every panel on each pass. CAVEAT: these milliseconds are harness time, not browser time — querySelectorAll and innerHTML parsing are native in a browser and plain JavaScript in the shim, so the absolute cost is lower in the deck. What the measurement establishes is the RANKING (the most expensive render on a clean load) and that every edit re-triggers it.

findings.system: tests/runtime-harness.js — what it does and does not prove
findings.description: The harness runs the script under a DOM shim, not a browser. It proves: the script reaches its last line, which container ids receive innerHTML, which $() targets are missing, which renderers throw and on which document shape, and how long each render takes. It does NOT prove layout, CSS, real clipboard/speech/canvas behaviour, cross-origin fetches, or the real artifact db capability — window.claude is absent unless injected. 50 of 61 sweep rows passed, 10 degraded, 1 failed. Treat a harness PASS as 'the script did not break', not as 'the dashboard looks right'.

findings.system: Bug found and fixed during testing
findings.category: Bug found and fixed during testing
findings.description: The first version of run()/run_sh() captured the command's exit status with `_rc=$?` after an `if cmd; then ... fi`. That reads the *if statement's* status, which is 0 on the else branch, so every failure returned 0 and was reported as INSTALLED. The sandbox run surfaced it: `npm install -g codeburn` failed with SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN and the script printed 'INSTALLED codeburn'. Fixed to `_rc=0; "$@" ... || _rc=$?`, and the two npm steps plus headroom, graphify and strix now additionally verify the binary is actually present before claiming success.
findings.fixRef: MAC-SETUP.sh run()/run_sh() capture the command's own exit status; binaries verified present before 'installed'

findings.description: The spec's property table named `Date` as the row key and did not list the `Day` property at all. The real database has both: `Day` is the Title property carrying `YYYY-MM-DD` and described in Notion as 'the row key'; `Date` is a separate Date property described as 'the calendar day this row covers'. A sync keyed on `Date` alone, or a phone-side write that leaves `Day` blank, produces rows with empty titles. The real database wins.

findings.system: Bug found and fixed during testing — mac-verify.sh
findings.category: Bug found and fixed during testing — mac-verify.sh
findings.description: The file-mode check originally tried BSD `stat -f '%OLp'` first with a GNU `stat -c '%a'` fallback. On Linux `stat -f` means 'file SYSTEM status' and SUCCEEDS, so the fallback never fired and a filesystem report was printed where a permission mode belonged. Now GNU-first with an octal-digits validation, then BSD. Also fixed: a `while read` loop over launchctl output inside a pipeline ran in a subshell, so its FAIL counts could never reach the exit code — rewritten as a heredoc loop.
findings.fixRef: mac-verify.sh filemode() GNU-first with octal validation; heredoc loop — F-V2-30 confirms the trap is handled

findings.description: limit-samples.log is an ungated sink for task output. Neither the state directory nor the log has an enforced mode, no rotation, and no retention limit, while the script does enforce chmod 600 on the .env next to it.

findings.description: claude-auto.sh's chmod-600 check on the .env uses a BSD-first stat fallback that is wrong on Linux, and the correct implementation already exists elsewhere in this repo. On GNU coreutils `stat -f` means 'file SYSTEM status': it prints a filesystem report to stdout, and because command substitution captures stdout from BOTH sides of the `||`, the filesystem report is concatenated with the real mode and the case never matches. The whole free-fallback path then refuses to run on any Linux host.
findings.fixRef: reproduced by execution in brain aa3b734's session; no fix committed — do not point the runner at claude-auto until fixed

The one field derived from untrusted text (reason) IS correctly sanitised, so the exposure is the file's permissions, not its content.

findings.description: FR5b's LaunchAgent plist puts $HOME/.npm-global/bin on PATH, i.e. this Mac uses a custom npm prefix; uv tool and pipx shims land in ~/.local/bin. Both are commonly absent from a non-login shell's PATH, which made presence checks re-install tools that were already there. Both scripts now look in ~/.local/bin and `npm root -g` before concluding a tool is missing, and mac-verify.sh reports 'installed but not on PATH' as NEEDS-STEVEN rather than as a broken install. Neither script edits a shell rc file to fix PATH — that is Steven's dotfile.
findings.fixRef: both scripts look in ~/.local/bin and npm root -g; 'installed but not on PATH' reported as NEEDS-STEVEN
